column5: We adopt the World3 model of Meadows et al. (1972) to simulate water demand.
Concerns about exponential growth have a long history (Meadows et al. 1972).
Meadows et al. (1972) correctly identified the tension between growth and resources.
The collapse predictions of Meadows et al. (1972) rested on implausibly static assumptions.
Commoner (1971) argued for an ecological reorganization of industry.
Like Meadows et al. (1972), Commoner (1971) emphasized planetary limits.
Schumacher (1974) provided a normative critique of growth economics.
We extend Schumacher's (1974) framework to include digital labor.
A natural next step is to revisit the scenarios of Meadows et al. (1972) with updated data.
Several authors warned of ecological limits (e.g., Commoner 1971; Meadows et al. 1972).
Schumacher's (1974) appropriate-technology argument has shaped development discourse.
The seminal Limits to Growth study (Meadows et al. 1972) initiated modern sustainability research.
